meta.title: retreats | Alaya Ecolodge
meta.description: Alaya hosts retreats and trainings on various topics related to wellness and sustainability, offering vegan or vegetarian food.

intro.heading: A Quiet Green Oasis
intro.text: Alaya is a haven of harmony and heritage. Our beautifully restored wooden cottages reflect mindful living and Balinese cultural values. Guests often describe the energy here as healing and magical, a place where nature's rhythms nourish the spirit.

paths.title: Join a Program
paths.text: Looking to deepen your practice or attend a training in a natural, nurturing environment? Alaya offers a peaceful venue ideal for retreats and transformational learning. Nestled in the tranquil village of Pemuteran, far from tourist crowds, Alaya is the perfect base for retreat, reflection, and renewal.

paths.title: Hold a Retreat
paths.text: We welcome facilitators and educators to hold retreats at Alaya. Our ecolodge can host up to 25 participants, with optional vegetarian or vegan catering. Whether you bring your own itinerary or collaborate with us to design one, we’re here to support you every step of the way.

programmes.title: Truth Based Relationships Retreat

description.text: Escape to the nature of Bali for a transformative retreat based on the Authentic Relationships Model by its author Psychologist Juan Andres Papagno Gazmuri. Learn to navigate connections with friends, partners, family and co-workers from a place of deep personal truth. Embodying your authentic self begins here.

description.text: This 14-day immersive wellbeing journey is designed for anyone seeking balance and clarity through practices like yoga, breathwork, and nature connection. No prior experience is required to join this path toward reconnection and self-understanding.

description.text: Join us on this one-week exploration of Yoga and Balinese culture. programmes.title: Ecovillage Design Education (EDE)

description.text: Join a global movement of changemakers in this 4-week immersive program certified by

and recognized by UNESCO as a ‘Contributor to Education for Sustainable Development’. The EDE explores the four dimensions of sustainable community design: social, ecological, economic, and worldview. Through hands-on learning, field visits, and collaboration, participants design solutions for regenerative living

programmes.title: Yoga  Teacher  Training Course (TTC)

description.text: This 200-hour Yoga Alliance certified program with Bala Yoga School blends traditional wisdom with modern practice. Participants will deepen their understanding of asana, pranayama, meditation, chanting, anatomy, and yogic philosophy. Set in the tranquil surroundings of Alaya, this TTC offers a nurturing space to develop your personal practice and teaching skills.

paragraphs.text: An enriching month-long immersion into yoga practice and philosophy. This TTC guided students in developing a strong, injury-free self-practice and prepared them to teach with confidence and clarity. Mornings began with pranayama and chanting, followed by asana, meditation sessions, and integral yoga theory lessons: all in Alaya’s peaceful natural setting.

paragraphs.text: This series of 3-day workshops introduced participants to the principles of Ayurveda, focusing on personalized nutrition using local, affordable ingredients. The sessions included both theory and hands-on cooking, aiming to reconnect people with the healing potential of food. Delivered in English and Indonesian, the workshops supported local knowledge-sharing through scholarships.

paragraphs.text: The training took place four times over 3 days in 2024, with 4 - 6 participants including international students and local students. They were all level 1 trainings, giving a solid introduction to basic massage including techniques from Thai Yoga, Ayurveda and Siddha medecine.
The students were given a book to keep practicing until they would be ready for level 2.

paragraphs.text: A 4 week transformative experience that brought together changemakers, educators, and ecologists from around the world. Participants engaged in hands-on design practices rooted in sustainability, systems thinking, and regenerative living. The 2024 and 2025 cohort left inspired to build communities that nurture both people and the planet. We also hosted a "Training of Trainers" in 2025 as many Indonesian and International participants were keen on moving into Gaia Education and facilitators training.
